status.note: Only meaningful inside a Tabs. The tab half of the pair; TabPanel is the other, and both are members of the same collection — which the schema cannot say.

intent.purpose: One tab: a label that reveals its panel when chosen. It carries its own identity and its own disabled state, and nothing else.
behaviour: Compares its value against the selection on the surrounding Tabs to decide whether it is chosen.
Chooses itself on click, and on Space or Enter when focused.
Cannot un-choose itself. A tab strip always has exactly one chosen tab.
Points at the panel of the same value, and is pointed back at by it.
Throws if rendered outside a Tabs.
notFor: Acting as a link. It renders a button and changes no URL — a tab that navigates is a nav item.
Holding the panel's content. Keeping them apart is what lets panels live outside the tablist, which the tablist role requires.

selected.description: Derived from the surrounding Tabs by comparing value. Not settable here.
selected.visual: An indicator appears along the bottom edge and the label takes its selected colour.

disabled.description: Set by the prop or inherited from the strip. Skipped by arrow-key movement.
disabled.visual: The label takes the disabled colour and the pointer cursor is dropped.

hover.description: The pointer is over the tab and it is not disabled.
hover.visual: The label takes its hover colour.

focus-visible.description: Focused in a way the browser judges worth showing a ring for.
focus-visible.visual: A ring is drawn inside the tab's box.

a11y.keyboard: Reachable with Tab only when chosen. Arrow keys on the strip move here and choose in one action.
notes: The accessible name is whatever is passed as the label. A tab given a non-text child has no name and nothing detects that.
disabled renders a natively disabled button, so a keyboard user cannot land on it to discover it exists.
The chosen state must not be carried by colour alone. The indicator is the non-colour signal.
This tab points at a panel that may not be rendered. Nothing here checks that a panel of the same value exists, and a tab referencing a missing id is reported by some assistive technology.

label.description: The tab's name. Fills the label part.

root.description: The tab. Owns the focus ring, the hit area and the indicator.

indicator.description: The bar along the bottom edge marking the chosen tab. Out of flow, so its arrival moves nothing.
